method: Plan a round basket as rows of weavers climbing a wall that interpolates linearly between the base and rim diameters. Rows are the wall height divided by the reed width, rounded to the nearest whole row, because each row of weavers advances the weave by about one reed width; the rounded height is reported so a wall that lands short of the request is visible. Each row takes the diameter at its mid-height, base plus the rim-minus-base difference times the row centre fraction, and its weft length is pi times that diameter times one plus the weave slack percentage, which pays for going over and under the stakes. The sum over all rows equals pi times the slack factor times the rows times the mean of the base and rim diameters, evaluated with an explicit per-row loop. Stake length is the slanted wall length, the square root of the wall height squared plus half the rim-minus-base difference squared, plus four reed widths past the rim for the border. Stake reed is the stake count times that length. The rim figure covers a three-rod wale: three weavers, each once around the rim, at pi times the rim diameter times the slack factor. Totals are converted to metres at 1000 mm and to feet at 304.8 mm per foot. Stakes must be an even whole number from 6 to 64 so pairs cross at the base, and the plan is refused when the stakes would sit closer than twice the reed width at the base, naming the measured spacing. Inputs are decimal millimetres and percent; blank, non-numeric, exponent, negative, multiple-decimal-point and out-of-range values are refused with the failing field named. Warnings cover fewer than three rows, a wall leaning more than 40 degrees from vertical, a rounded wall that differs from the requested height by more than 12 percent, rim spacing growing more than 60 percent, and stakes tighter than three reed widths. The page computes text only, stores nothing and makes no network requests.

sources.title: Basket weaving practice: a three-rod wale passes three weavers around the rim, and stakes are turned down past the rim to form the border.
Round reed is sold by diameter, so a #3 reed wove as a weaver advances the wall by about 3 mm per row.
Right-triangle geometry: the slanted wall length is the hypotenuse of the wall height and half the difference between the rim and base diameters.
